title: Lanthanide Compounds with Fluorinated OC6F5 Ligands: Homo- and Heterovalent Complexes of Eu(II) and Eu(III)

material_class.structural_family: linear Eu(II) phenoxide trimer with six bridging OC6F5 ligands

synthesis.procedure: Under ultrapure nitrogen using dry-box or Schlenk techniques, Eu metal (0.15 g, 1.0 mmol), HOC6F5 (0.31 g, 1.67 mmol), and Hg (0.025 g, 0.12 mmol) were added to DME (20 mL) and stirred for two weeks at room temperature to give a green-gray solution with a black precipitate. The solution was filtered; the filtrate was concentrated to around 8 mL and layered with hexane (20 mL) to give pale yellow lathes (0.21 g, 40%) of 1.
synthesis.vessel_or_method: dry box or Schlenk techniques under ultrapure nitrogen
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: filtered; filtrate concentrated to ~8 mL and layered with hexane (20 mL) to give pale yellow lathes

properties.summary: Divalent 1 is yellow in solution and as a DME adduct; no UV-vis absorption maxima were observed between 300 and 750 nm in DME or pyridine. Pyridine displacement produces a deep orange Eu-to-pyridine CT color without a quantified absorption maximum. Crystal color alone is not treated as an optical measurement.

measurements.name: UV-vis absorption maxima
measurements.conditions: 300–750 nm; DME or pyridine; 1.0 mm quartz cell

source_locations.location: Experimental Section UV-vis of 1; electronic-properties discussion

material_class.structural_family: monomeric Eu(III) pentafluorophenoxide with two DME ligands

synthesis.procedure: Method A: under nitrogen, Eu metal (0.13 g, 0.84 mmol), PhSSPh (0.29 g, 1.3 mmol), and Hg (0.025 g, 0.12 mmol) were added to DME (20 mL) and stirred for 7 days to give a yellow solution with a yellow-green precipitate. C6F5OH (0.46 g, 2.56 mmol) was added, and the mixture was stirred for two weeks, then filtered. The bright yellow filtrate was concentrated to about 4 mL and layered with hexane (25 mL) to give yellow rod-shaped crystals of 2 (0.24 g, 32%). Method B: Eu metal (0.15 g, 1.0 mmol), C6F5OH (0.55 g, 3.0 mmol), and Hg (0.010 g, 0.05 mmol) in DME (20 mL) were stirred for 5 days, filtered, concentrated to about 8 mL, and layered with hexane (15 mL) to give 2 (0.36 g, 42%).

properties.summary: Trivalent 2 is light yellow. UV-vis in DME shows weak f–f absorptions at 575 and 529 nm; no well-defined MLCT maxima in pyridine. The phenoxide LMCT is shifted into the UV.

measurements.conditions: DME; ε = 9×10^-2 L mol^-1 cm^-1; 1.0 mm quartz cell

synthesis.procedure: Method A: under nitrogen, Eu metal (0.14 g, 0.92 mmol), PhSSPh (0.205 g, 0.94 mmol), and Hg (0.03 g, 0.15 mmol) were added to DME (20 mL) and stirred at room temperature for 2 days to give a yellow solution and green precipitate. C6F5OH (0.33 g, 1.79 mmol) was added and stirring continued for 6 days. Filtration separated a yellow-orange solution from a red-orange precipitate. The filtrate was concentrated to 8 mL and layered with 15 mL of hexanes to give yellow-orange crystals of 3 (0.34 g, 63%). Method B: Eu metal (0.076 g, 0.50 mmol), C6F5OH (0.230 g, 1.25 mmol), and Hg (0.015 g, 0.075 mmol) in DME (20 mL) were stirred for 3 days, filtered, concentrated to 8 mL, and layered with hexanes (15 mL) to give 3 (0.096 g, 26%).

properties.summary: Heterovalent 3 is deeper colored in the solid state than homovalent 1 and 2, attributed to possible Eu(II)→Eu(III) intervalence excitation. UV-vis in DME shows weak f–f peaks at 575 and 529 nm, essentially identical to 2; no well-defined MLCT maxima in pyridine.
